_comment: The question the relevance screen asks per (claim, work) pair, by
R/build_llm_relevance_screen.R. Sibling of jev_claim_questions.json, which
holds Phase 1's.
Tracked as a format = 'file' target, so EDITING THIS FILE INVALIDATES SCORING.
`version` below is what enforces that: the screen discards any row scored under
a lower version before its resume diff. Resumability is keyed on the pair, so
without the bump an edit would leave every existing row looking done. BUMP IT
whenever instructions or criteria change in meaning.
A NOUL, not a Choice, unlike Phase 1. The question has one axis -- does this
paper bear on the claim at all -- with no competing options to distribute
probability across. The skill: 'Noul: whether a condition holds ... probability
of yes'. Phase 1 uses Choice because its three labels are mutually exclusive
and compete.
THE PAPER GOES IN instructions.paper, NOT in the shared state. Question ids are
for code and are never sent to the model, so a question keyed by work_id against
a state full of papers cannot say which paper it means -- the model answers
about the chunk. That was version 1, and it produced 170,405 rows in which 7,889
works under one claim share 23 distinct values. Those are archived under
deep_archive/2026-10-05_relevance_v1_chunk_level/.
WHY THIS QUESTION EXISTS AT ALL. quote_is_verbatim() checks that a quote OCCURS
in the premise, never that it BEARS on the claim -- found in real data, not
hypothesised: REFUTES verdicts citing verbatim but topically adjacent sentences,
every one passing the verbatim check.
ITS FUTURE IS OPEN. Under a jev Phase 1 this duplicates part of the Choice's own
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO criterion: measured on 2,000 routed pairs, p_nei and
(1 - addresses) agree on 95.4% of keep/drop calls, Spearman 0.781. Left in for
the first KM C. run because it costs $0.65 and produces the population that test
lacked -- pairs Jev itself routed. See design_notes.md point 9.

question.instructions_question: Does this paper address the specific subject of the claim closely enough that its findings bear on whether the claim is true?

criteria.true: the paper studies the same phenomenon, taxa, driver or region the claim is about, and its findings speak to the claim
criteria.false: the paper is about a related but different topic, so its findings cannot settle the claim either way
